claims.text: The long, narrow, glacier-carved sea inlets along Norway's coast are called fjords.
Atolls, estuaries and lagoons are different coastal features, not glacier-carved inlets.
Fjords formed where glaciers carved deep U-shaped valleys that the sea later flooded.
Chile, New Zealand and Canada also have fjords.

evidence.restatement: Norway's long, steep-sided, glacier-cut sea inlets are fjords.
Atolls are coral rings, estuaries are river mouths and lagoons are sheltered shallow waters; none is a glacial inlet.
Fjords are glacial U-shaped valleys drowned by the sea after the ice retreated.
Chile, New Zealand and Canada also have fjord coasts.
Fjords are long, narrow, deep sea inlets carved by glaciers, typical of Norway's coast.
Atolls are coral rings, estuaries are river mouths and lagoons are shallow coastal waters: none is a glacier-carved inlet.
Glaciers cut deep U-shaped valleys that the sea floods when the ice melts, forming fjords.
Chile, New Zealand and Canada all have fjords.
